messages:
maria: FYI, abnormal compaction activity hitting ap-southeast1 and ap-northeast1. Small inference workers are being bounced and contiguous GPU slot availability dropped ~18% since 09:12 UTC. Tail latencies spiking for tiny requests.
kevin: what component initiated the compaction? scheduler, descheduler, or a custom compactor?
sam: looks like the new telemetry-driven compaction lambda rolled at 09:10 UTC. It's marking 'anchorless' pods as preferred eviction candidates to consolidate NVLINK groups.
maria: problem: our warm-pool pods intentionally have no node anchors so they remain schedulable anywhere. The telemetry heuristic treats that as low-anchoring and evicts them, which defeats the warm-pool purpose.
anya: ugh. That interaction was overlooked in the experiment plan. Are there log lines we can see?
maria: pasted a few lines from the compactor controller log:
```
2026-03-21T09:12:58Z compactor/controller: evaluate pod default/worker-mini-22 score=0.12 (anchorless, low-kv-hit)
2026-03-21T09:13:01Z compactor/controller: evicting pod node=gpux-ase1 id=worker-mini-22 reason=telemetry-compact-priority
2026-03-21T09:13:10Z compactor/controller: evaluate pod k8s-warmpool/warmer-7 score=0.09 (anchorless)
2026-03-21T09:13:11Z compactor/controller: evicting pod node=gpux-ane1 id=warmer-7 reason=telemetry-compact-priority
```
kevin: that "telemetry-compact-priority" tag is the new metric. It's intended to evict low-cache-hit and cross-rack pods, but it shouldn't touch warmpools.
sam: immediate mitigation: patch compactor config to exclude namespaces `k8s-warmpool` and pods with label `redwood/warmpool=true`. We can roll to ap-southeast1 canary first.
anya: longer term we should invert the heuristic: instead of treating anchorless as low-priority globally, require an explicit opt-in label for compaction like `redwood/compact-eligible=true`. That avoids surprising evictions.
maria: agreed. Quick plan I propose: 1) Canary patch to exclude warmpool namespace (saves current churn). 2) Autoscaler change to add `redwood/warmpool=true` label to warm-pool pods. 3) Change compactor to require `redwood/compact-eligible=true` for eviction unless persistence window exceeded.
kevin: I'll push the canary exclude now to ap-southeast1, rollout id rld-20260321-09:48. Watching evictions metric and `gpu.contiguous_slots`.
infra-bot: [alert] compactor: 2026-03-21T09:13:00Z -> 2026-03-21T09:30:00Z: 420 evictions across clusters (rule=telemetry-compact-priority)
maria: impact estimate: ~420 evicted warmpool/anchorless pods, ~14% tail latency increase for small inference; extra 6% CPU/GPU churn on autoscaler churn (cold-starts).
sam: small followups: add a 5m persistence requirement to the compactor before it evicts anchorless pods, and only evict if contiguous slot improvement >= 2 GPUs. Cuts noise.
anya: I'll draft the compact-eligibility label RFC this afternoon. Also adding a runbook note: experiments that classify pods by implicit metadata MUST whitelist warmpools.
kevin: canary looks good so far; evictions dropped to near-zero in the last 6m. I'll promote to global in 20m if no regressions.
maria: thanks. Opening INFRA-2026-ticket: compactor opt-in + warmpool protection. Assigning to sam/anya.
sam: I'll open the autoscaler PR to label warmpool pods with `redwood/warmpool=true` and add a unit test for the label.
kevin: also add a Prom rule to flag compactor evictions that target `k8s-warmpool` specifically so we catch regressions.
anya: sounds good. Adding the change to the telemetry experiment checklist: "exclude warmpools and require opt-in label for anchorless eviction."
maria: closing loop here. If anyone sees new evictions or tail latency creeping back up, ping this thread and we'll roll back the compactor. :pray:
